+medial paths, writes 21 ordinary brush strokes, and leaves the brush raised.

+def thin_target(mask: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Zhang-Suen thinning; gives one-pixel medial paths from the exemplar."""
+    s = mask.copy()
+    while True:
+        changed = False
+        for phase in (0, 1):
+            p = np.pad(s, 1, constant_values=False)
+            p2, p3 = p[:-2, 1:-1], p[:-2, 2:]
+            p4, p5 = p[1:-1, 2:], p[2:, 2:]
+            p6, p7 = p[2:, 1:-1], p[2:, :-2]
+            p8, p9 = p[1:-1, :-2], p[:-2, :-2]
+            count = (p2.astype(np.uint8) + p3 + p4 + p5 + p6 + p7 + p8 + p9)
+            ring = (p2, p3, p4, p5, p6, p7, p8, p9, p2)
+            transitions = np.zeros_like(s, dtype=np.uint8)
+            for a, b in zip(ring[:-1], ring[1:]):
+                transitions += (~a & b)
+            if phase == 0:
+                condition = (~(p2 & p4 & p6)) & (~(p4 & p6 & p8))
+            else:
+                condition = (~(p2 & p4 & p8)) & (~(p2 & p6 & p8))
+            remove = s & (count >= 2) & (count <= 6) & (transitions == 1) & condition
+            if remove.any():
+                s[remove] = False
+                changed = True
+        if not changed:

+def build_centerlines():
+    gray = np.asarray(Image.open(TARGET).convert("L"))
+    mask = gray < 100

+    h, w = skel.shape

+
+    # Graph adjacency avoids redundant diagonal edges next to a cardinal edge.
+    adjacency = {}

+        for dv in (-1, 0, 1):
